what: PRB-1420, fourth and last part: every needs_review observation of occupation-full-publication-2026-10-27-v1 left after parts 1 to 3 (252 rows: identity questions, psalm superscriptions, titles of address and the rest), decided by reading the verses; and the owner's answers to part 3's questions applied. Admitted claims are in ../person-occupations.json; this file says why, and why not. Requests and the loader never read it.
rules: The rules of parts 1 to 3 hold (prb-1420-part-1.json to prb-1420-part-3.json).

Identity is the records' question: the occupation follows the record the verse's word is annotated to (part 2). A row asking whether two names are one man is covered where the annotated record already holds the occupation, admitted where it does not and the verse says it, and refused for a record the word does not name.
A psalm's superscription (לְ with a name) names no office, and 'psalmist' or 'author' is no occupation; לַמְנַצֵּחַ addresses the choirmaster.
συνεργός 'fellow worker' is a relation to Paul; 'man of God' and 'servant of the LORD' are honorifics; Pharisee and Zealot are parties.
A title of address (Διδάσκαλε, Ῥαββί) or a confession ('the Christ') adds nothing to the role the narrator's own verb gives (Teacher), and no office King for Jesus (owner, 2026-11-09).
Jesus' mediation and advocacy are the ministry of the heavenly High priest he holds (Heb 7:25, 8:6), not further roles.

A practice the narrator says of a person with the verb counts by the measure the owner used for Simon of Samaria (Acts 8:9 μαγεύων): Manasseh, 2 Chr 33:6 וְכִשֵּׁף. Hostile speech (Jehu of Jezebel, 2 Kgs 9:22) does not.
Heavenly beings the text calls שַׂר of a kingdom (Dan 10:13, 20) hold a heavenly role (owner, 2026-10-27, TSK-1254).

admitted.why: Col 4:17 'take heed to the ministry (διακονίαν) which thou hast received in the Lord, that thou fulfil it': a ministry received and to be fulfilled, said of him by Paul; the stated service counts (part 1), as διάκονος does for Timothy (1 Thess 3:2).

2 Sam 23:33 'Shammah the Hararite' in the list of David's mighty men (23:8, the Thirty from 23:24, 'thirty and seven in all' 23:39): BHSA, KJV and the Greek list him as one of them, and the word is annotated to this record. BSB reads 'Jonathan son of Shammah the Hararite' after 1 Chr 11:34 'Jonathan son of Shage', which the records also join to him; admitted on the Hebrew's list, as part 1 admitted Oded on BHSA's reading of 2 Chr 15:8 beside BSB's Azariah.

Dan 10:20 'and lo, the prince (שַׂר) of Greece shall come', in the angel's word of his fight with the prince of Persia, beside Michael 'one of the chief princes' and 'your prince' (10:13, 21): the noun of rank said of a heavenly being, so a heavenly role (owner, 2026-10-27, TSK-1254).

Dan 10:13 'the prince (שַׂר) of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days; but lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me', and 10:20: the noun of rank said of a heavenly being, so a heavenly role (owner, 2026-10-27, TSK-1254).

Gen 36:24 'this is Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness as he pastured (בִּרְעֹתוֹ) the donkeys of Zibeon his father': the shepherd's verb רָעָה said of him as his work in his father's house, as of Rachel (Gen 29:9) and Moses (Exod 3:1).
